faq.answer: The facet describes a personality tendency. A depressive disorder is a clinical condition assessed with broader criteria, duration, severity, and impairment.
faq.question: How is the Big Five Depression facet different from depressive disorder?

faq.answer: A trait score cannot decide. Consider qualified support when low mood is persistent, severe, distressing, or interferes with daily functioning.
faq.question: Do I need to see a clinician?

faq.answer: Yes. A tendency is not a permanent state and does not eliminate positive emotion, meaning, connection, or recovery.
faq.question: Can someone with stronger Depression feel happy?

faq.answer: This package provides no basis for inferring creativity from the facet. Avoid romanticizing suffering or treating it as a creative requirement.
faq.question: Is the Depression facet related to creativity?

faq.answer: This page does not provide an individual genetic estimate or causal explanation. Personality reflects many interacting influences.

sections.body:
The Depression facet describes proneness to sadness, discouragement, and low mood. The inherited technical label must not be read as a diagnosis of depression or any other disorder.

“Depression within Neuroticism: tendency toward sadness and discouragement” is used on this page as a descriptive construct within the NEO/IPIP-NEO 30-facet framework. The official IPIP resource describes scales that measure constructs similar to NEO facets and lists item mappings ([S11](https://ipip.ori.org/Finding_Scales_to_Measure_Particular_Constructs.htm)); this does not make scores from different instruments, translations, or products interchangeable.

FermatMind has not published product-level reliability, validity, Chinese norms, or individual predictive evidence for the score discussed on this page. This material is for self-observation and education. It is not for clinical diagnosis, hiring screening, school admission, or replacing a career decision.

> **Content method and update:** FermatMind Editorial prepared this page with AI-assisted drafting and checked terminology, boundaries, and evidence against public personality-psychology sources. It is for self-understanding and education; it is not clinical diagnosis, hiring screening, or individual-outcome prediction. Substantive update: 2026-07-19; review mode: solo_operator; not clinically reviewed.
sections.heading: Evidence and Interpretation Boundaries

sections.body: A stronger tendency means disappointment, loss, or discouraging interpretations may pull mood downward more readily or for longer. A weaker tendency means low mood may occur less readily or recovery may feel faster. Neither end establishes a clinical condition, emotional depth, or immunity from depression.
sections.heading: Precise Definition

sections.body: Depression belongs to [Neuroticism](/en/personality/big-five/neuroticism). It concerns sadness and discouragement, one component of negative emotional sensitivity.
sections.heading: Parent Domain

sections.body:
- **Depression versus depressive disorder:** A disorder requires clinical assessment of symptoms, duration, severity, context, and functioning; this trait page cannot provide it.
- **Depression versus Anxiety:** Depression concerns a downward emotional tone; [Anxiety](/en/personality/big-five/facets/anxiety) concerns anticipated threat and worry.
- **Depression versus Vulnerability:** Depression concerns low mood; [Vulnerability](/en/personality/big-five/facets/vulnerability) concerns difficulty coping under pressure.
sections.heading: Distinguishing Neighboring Facets

sections.body: Possible cues include becoming discouraged after setbacks, dwelling on loss, needing longer to regain emotional momentum, or expecting less reward after disappointment. Weaker Depression may appear as quicker mood recovery. Grief, illness, discrimination, isolation, sleep loss, and current circumstances can create similar observations.
sections.heading: Behavioral Cues

sections.body: Someone may be resilient after work setbacks yet deeply affected by relationship loss. A cheerful public style can coexist with private sadness, and temporary low mood can occur at any trait level. Duration and functional impact require attention beyond a personality label.
sections.heading: Contextual Differences

sections.body:
- Feeling discouragement strongly after a setback.
- Taking longer to regain emotional momentum.
- Noticing loss and limitation readily.
- Withdrawing while mood is low.
- Finding hope less accessible during strain.
sections.heading: Possible Expressions When Stronger

sections.body:
- Recovering emotional momentum relatively quickly.
- Maintaining hope after disappointment.
- Experiencing sadness without a prolonged downward pull.
- Underestimating another person’s recovery needs.
- Appearing steady during loss while still grieving privately.
sections.heading: Possible Expressions When Weaker

sections.body: Stronger Depression may support sensitivity to loss and a realistic acknowledgment of pain, while costs may include prolonged discouragement or withdrawal. Weaker Depression can support recovery, but it is not proof of resilience or mental health. No level establishes creativity, depth, diagnosis, treatment need, or prognosis.
sections.heading: Strengths and Costs

sections.body: After a rejected proposal, a designer feels discouraged for several days and doubts the value of the entire project. She asks a colleague to separate the specific feedback from her global conclusion, then schedules one small revision. The pattern is informative without becoming an identity.
sections.heading: An Original Case

sections.body: A generally upbeat teacher experiences a major depressive episode and seeks clinical care. A weaker personality tendency does not prevent a disorder, just as a stronger tendency does not diagnose one.
sections.heading: An Original Counterexample

sections.body:
1. Which setbacks pull your mood down most reliably?
2. How long does emotional momentum usually take to return?
3. Do you turn one disappointment into a global conclusion?
4. What changes in sleep, contact, or routine accompany low mood?
5. When does a pattern exceed self-observation and warrant support?
sections.heading: Self-Observation Questions

sections.body: After one ordinary disappointment, write the specific event, the broad conclusion your mind produced, and one next action that remains possible. This is not treatment. Seek qualified help if low mood is persistent, severe, affects functioning, or includes thoughts of self-harm; use local emergency support for immediate danger.
sections.heading: Low-Risk Action Experiment

sections.body: Return to [Neuroticism](/en/personality/big-five/neuroticism) or the [30-facet guide](/en/personality/big-five/facets). Continue with [Anxiety](/en/personality/big-five/facets/anxiety), [Anger](/en/personality/big-five/facets/anger), [Self-Consciousness](/en/personality/big-five/facets/self-consciousness), [Impulsiveness](/en/personality/big-five/facets/impulsiveness), and [Vulnerability](/en/personality/big-five/facets/vulnerability).
